name: Microcystic Stromal Tumor

prevalence.estimate: extremely rare, fewer than 100 cases reported

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Microcystic Stromal Tumor

criteria.description: Presence of microcystic, solid, and hyalinized fibrous stroma pattern on histology
Immunohistochemical positivity for beta-catenin (nuclear and cytoplasmic) and CD10
Lack of expression of inhibin, calretinin, and epithelial markers
Presentation as a unilateral ovarian mass, often asymptomatic or with abdominal discomfort

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of microcystic stromal pattern with positive beta-catenin immunostaining and absence of inhibin/calretinin expression
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for CTNNB1 mutations may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral ovarian mass with microcystic stromal architecture
pathognomonic.notes: Detected via imaging or surgical exploration
searchTerms: one-sided ovarian lump with small cysts
ovarian mass with tiny cyst structures

common.notes: May be detected on physical examination

rare.symptomName: Acute abdominal pain due to tumor rupture or torsion
searchTerms: sudden belly pain from tumor twist
acute abdominal pain from mass rupture
sharp stomach pain due to tumor complications

rare.notes: Extremely rare and not well characterized

laboratory: No elevation of inhibin or alpha-fetoprotein
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing unilateral ovarian mass with cystic and solid components
other: Histopathology showing microcystic, solid, and fibrous stromal components
Immunohistochemistry positive for beta-catenin (nuclear and cytoplasmic), CD10; negative for inhibin and calretinin

distinguishingFeatures: Spindle cell morphology without microcystic pattern

redFlags: Signs of ovarian torsion (acute severe abdominal pain)
Evidence of tumor rupture or hemorrhage
references: Prat J. Ovarian tumors with microcystic stromal pattern: a review. Int J Gynecol Pathol. 2014.
Sheng W, et al. Microcystic stromal tumor of the ovary: clinicopathologic and molecular analysis. Am J Surg Pathol. 2016.
